# Starter Kit documentation (/)



The kit puts an Exasol database on this computer and sets it up for the work you do. What it sets up depends on your **persona**. Pick a section below, or in the list at the top of the sidebar.

<Cards>
  <Card title="All personas" href="/kit">
    The kit itself: what a persona is, loading data, column maps, add-ons and every command.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Data Scientist" href="/data-scientist">
    Four notebooks and nine steps: load data, agree what each column means, explore, model, ask questions and share.
  </Card>
</Cards>

## From a notebook [#from-a-notebook]

```python
import exakit.nb as nb

nb.docs()                  # your persona's section, under the cell
nb.docs("descriptor")      # search
nb.docs(nb.describe)       # one command's page
```

`nb.docs()` opens the section of the persona whose notebook you are in.


# FAQ (/data-scientist/faq)



<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="Do I need a terminal?">
    No. Everything the notebooks need runs from a cell or a card: `nb.kit_check()`, `nb.exakit(...)`, `nb.addon_ready(...)`. See [Run the kit from a notebook](/data-scientist/guides/run-the-kit).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Do I need an AI model?">
    No. Every step runs without one. A model is used only to draft SQL in Ask and to sort texts into themes, and both are off until you turn them on. Ask also has a drafter with no model: `nb.draft_question`.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Is my data sent anywhere?">
    Not by default. The database and the notebooks run on this computer. With a model set up, Ask sends the column map and your question, never rows. The themes step sends a sample of texts, and asks first when the data is a live external source.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="What is a column map?">
    The column map gives every column in a table its role. Its technical name in the code is the descriptor. See [Column map and approval](/data-scientist/concepts/descriptor).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Who is the approver?">
    You are. The kit proposes roles; a person approves them. A model never approves, and the kit never chooses the target.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Why does a notebook say my data is not approved?">
    Explore, Ask and Share read only an approved column map. Open `00_quickstart`, review the map and approve it. See [Review and approve the column map](/data-scientist/guides/approve-column-map).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How do I switch to another dataset?">
    Approve it in the quickstart. With `DATASET = None`, the other notebooks follow the dataset approved last when you run their first cell again. Or set `DATASET = "..."` in a notebook to pin one.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Can I use my own table?">
    Yes. Load a file with `nb.load_own_file(...)`, or use a table already in the database with `nb.use_table(...)`. See [Load data](/data-scientist/guides/load-data).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Does preparing the data change my table?">
    No. The checks only read. The joined view and the typed view are views in `EXAKIT_PREPARED`, created only when you ask.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Can an AI-drafted query change my data?">
    No. Nothing runs until you approve the exact text, and approved questions run as the read-only user.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Where is my work saved?">
    Under `~/.exasol-starter-kit`: column maps, workflow logs and hand-off bundles. See [Where things live](/data-scientist/develop/where-things-live).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Will an update overwrite my notebooks?">
    No. A notebook you edited is never overwritten, and one you deleted is not copied back.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="JupyterLab or Marimo?">
    Either. The same notebooks ship for both. `exakit notebook` opens JupyterLab and `exakit notebook marimo` opens Marimo.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How do I find a command?">
    `nb.docs("words")` searches these docs, and `nb.docs(nb.some_command)` opens that command's page. [All commands](/data-scientist/reference) lists every one.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>


# Data Scientist notebooks (/data-scientist)



The Data Scientist persona gives you four notebooks that run on the Exasol database on this computer. They are one path with nine steps: get the data in, agree what each column means, prepare, explore, train and check a small model, ask questions in plain language, share a dashboard and hand the work off.

Every notebook opens with a **guided card** that does the page's steps with buttons and forms. Each card has a **Code** switch that shows the exact `exakit.nb` call behind every button, so anything you click you can also run in a cell.

## These docs, from a notebook [#these-docs-from-a-notebook]

```python
import exakit.nb as nb

nb.docs()                  # this site, under the cell
nb.docs("descriptor")      # search it
nb.docs(nb.describe)       # one command's page
nb.docs(browser=True)      # in a browser tab instead
```

The site is a folder of files that ships with the kit. `nb.docs()` serves it from this computer only, so reading and searching work without internet.

## What you need [#what-you-need]

Nothing beyond the kit. The persona installs the notebooks and their Python. An AI model is optional: every step except the AI ones runs without it.


# Troubleshooting (/data-scientist/troubleshooting)



## After an update, nothing changed [#after-an-update-nothing-changed]

Restart the kernel. A running kernel keeps the helpers it loaded before the update. In JupyterLab: **Kernel**, then **Restart Kernel**.

## "Step 1 approved ... after this page opened its data" [#step-1-approved--after-this-page-opened-its-data]

You approved a different dataset in the quickstart while this notebook was open. Run this notebook's first cell again and it switches to the newly approved dataset.

## A step says the column map is not approved [#a-step-says-the-column-map-is-not-approved]

The message is a `DescriptorNotApproved` error. Explore, Ask and Share do not read a draft. Open `00_quickstart` and approve the map. See [Review and approve the column map](/data-scientist/guides/approve-column-map).

## "... was not connected" [#-was-not-connected]

An external source could not be connected. The lines after it give the reason and a fix. The usual causes:

| Reason                                         | What to do                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The source refuses the connection or times out | Allow this computer's address at the source: a firewall rule, a security group or the server's own access list |
| Password or user refused                       | Check the user and enter the password again in the hidden box                                                  |
| A certificate cannot be verified               | Give the source's CA certificate in the optional settings                                                      |
| The schema is not found                        | Check the schema's name and case                                                                               |

Use **Test connection** first. It checks the inputs and reaches the source without changing anything.

## The database does not answer [#the-database-does-not-answer]

```python
nb.kit_check()          # is the database running?
nb.exakit("start")      # start it, for example after a restart of this computer
```

## An add-on is missing or stopped [#an-add-on-is-missing-or-stopped]

```python
nb.addon_ready("dash-server")
```

It installs the add-on when it is missing and starts it when it is stopped.

## A model step is skipped [#a-model-step-is-skipped]

No model is set, or the dataset has no column for that step. `nb.model_settings()` shows what is set. See [Set up a model](/data-scientist/guides/set-up-a-model).

## A text step is skipped [#a-text-step-is-skipped]

The dataset has no text column. `amazon_sales` and `fraud_transactions` have none, so the text model and the themes step skip on them and say so.

## The documentation does not open [#the-documentation-does-not-open]

`nb.docs()` reads the site from the kit copy. If it says the site is not there:

```python
nb.exakit("update", "notebook")
```

The documentation is served on this computer at one of the ports 8790 to 8809, the first one free. A port another program holds is skipped, and when all of them are taken any free port is used. To choose the port yourself, set `EXAKIT_DOCS_PORT` before starting the notebooks.

In a notebook that runs on another machine than your browser, the frame cannot reach the site. Use `nb.docs(browser=True)` on the machine that runs the kit.

## Find what a cell ran [#find-what-a-cell-ran]

```python
nb.show_sql()                              # the SQL the last query ran
nb.workflow_log(nb.current_workflow())     # everything this workflow did
```


# The kit and its personas (/kit)



The Exasol Personal Local Starter Kit installs a database on this computer and the tools around it. One command, `exakit`, runs all of it.

## What every install has [#what-every-install-has]

| Part          | What it is for                                                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The database  | Exasol, running on this computer                              |
| `exakit`      | The command that starts, checks, loads and updates everything |
| The AI bridge | Lets your AI clients query the database, read-only            |
| AI skills     | Instructions that teach an AI client how to use the kit       |
| Sample data   | Datasets to practise on                                       |

## What a persona adds [#what-a-persona-adds]

A **persona** is the kit set up for one kind of work. It decides which datasets are loaded, which add-ons are installed and which notebooks you get. See [What is a persona](/kit/personas/what-is-a-persona).

## Find your task [#find-your-task]

| I want to                                             | Go to                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| See or change which persona this kit is               | [Choose and change a persona](/kit/personas/choose-and-change) |
| Load a file, a folder or a kit dataset                | [Load data](/kit/data/load-data)                               |
| Say what each column of a table means                 | [Column maps](/kit/data/column-maps)                           |
| Run a query from the terminal                         | [Run SQL](/kit/data/run-sql)                                   |
| Install a dashboard server, notebooks or another tool | [Add-ons](/kit/tools/add-ons)                                  |
| Open JupyterLab or Marimo                             | [Notebooks](/kit/tools/notebooks)                              |
| See what a piece of work did, step by step            | [Workflows](/kit/tools/workflows)                              |
| Connect an AI client                                  | [AI clients and skills](/kit/tools/ai-clients-and-skills)      |
| Look up a command                                     | [All exakit commands](/kit/reference/commands)                 |
| Work through the Data Scientist notebooks             | [Data Scientist](/data-scientist)                              |

## Help on this computer [#help-on-this-computer]

```bash
exakit help                # every command
exakit help data-load      # one command in full
exakit catalog load        # search the commands
exakit status              # is the database up?
```

The same help is built into the kit, so it always matches the version you have.


# Add a command (/data-scientist/develop/add-a-command)



<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Write the helper [#write-the-helper]

    Add a function to a module in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/`, with a docstring. The first sentence becomes its one-line summary here; the rest becomes its reference text. Indented lines in a docstring are shown as code.

    Export it: import it in `exakit_nb/__init__.py` and add its name to `__all__`.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Put it in a notebook [#put-it-in-a-notebook]

    Add the call to the code section of the notebook it belongs to, guarded by a variable when it is optional:

    ```python
    if ADD_ON:
        nb.addon_ready(ADD_ON)
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Give a card a button for it [#give-a-card-a-button-for-it]

    Add one entry to `actions.ACTIONS` in `exakit_guide/actions.py`: the code and the notebook it belongs to. Have the screen call `actions.run(...)`.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Regenerate [#regenerate]

    ```bash
    python3 tools/notebooks.py --marimo     # the .ipynb and Marimo notebooks
    python3 tools/nb_docs.py                # the command reference
    ```

    The new helper now has an entry in its module's reference page and a row in [All commands](/data-scientist/reference). `nb.docs(nb.your_helper)` opens it once the site is rebuilt.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Test [#test]

    ```bash
    python3 -m unittest tests.test_notebook_guide tests.test_notebook_helpers tests.test_notebook_docs
    ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Callout>
  A whole new module gets its own reference page automatically, titled from its file name. Give it a proper title and a place in the order by adding one line to `PAGES` in `tools/nb_docs.py`.
</Callout>


# These docs (/data-scientist/develop/docs-site)



## How it works [#how-it-works]

* **Source:** MDX pages in `notebook/docs/content/docs/`, one folder per persona. The folder layout is the sidebar; each folder's `meta.json` sets its title and page order, and a persona's folder is marked `"root": true`, which makes it an entry in the list at the top of the sidebar.
* **Build:** a static site built with Node on a maintainer's machine. Users never need Node.
* **Shipped:** the built files, in `notebook/docs/site/`, travel with the kit.
* **Served:** `nb.docs()` serves that folder from the kit's own Python, on this computer only.

Search runs in the browser on an index inside the site. It forgives typos, matches as you type and needs no internet.

## Change a page [#change-a-page]

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Edit [#edit]

    Edit an `.mdx` file, or add one and list it in its folder's `meta.json`. Each page starts with:

    ```text
    ---
    title: Page title
    description: One sentence that says what the page covers.
    ---
    ```

    `Callout`, `Tabs`, `Steps`, `Cards` and `Accordions` are available on every page without imports.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Preview while you write [#preview-while-you-write]

    ```bash
    npm install
    ```

    ```bash
    npm run dev
    ```

    Run both in `notebook/docs`. The site is at `http://localhost:3000/docs` and reloads on every save.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Build and publish [#build-and-publish]

    ```bash
    npm run build
    ```

    ```bash
    python3 tools/nb_docs.py --publish
    ```

    The first writes `notebook/docs/out`; the second copies it to `notebook/docs/site` and stamps it with a digest of the sources.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Check [#check]

    ```bash
    python3 tools/nb_docs.py --check
    ```

    It fails when a generated page is stale, or when the shipped site was built from older sources than the ones in the repository.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Pages you do not edit [#pages-you-do-not-edit]

Everything under a persona's `reference/` folder is generated from the docstrings in `exakit_nb` by `python3 tools/nb_docs.py`. To change a command's text, change its docstring and run the tool.

## Links [#links]

Link to a page by its address, without the `/docs` prefix and without `.mdx`: `/data-scientist/concepts/descriptor`. Link to a command by its page and name: `/data-scientist/reference/describe#describe`. A test fails on a link that leads nowhere.


# How it fits together (/data-scientist/develop/how-it-fits)



## Three layers [#three-layers]

| Layer           | Where                                                    | What it owns                                                                  |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The kit         | `setup/`, the `exakit` command                           | The database, connections, loading, connectors, add-ons, the describe service |
| The helpers     | `notebook/package/exakit_nb/` (`import exakit.nb as nb`) | One Python call for each thing a notebook does                                |
| The guided view | `notebook/package/exakit_guide/` (`exakit.guide`)        | Cards that call the helpers; UI only                                          |

A notebook is cells that call the helpers. A card is a form that calls the same helpers. Neither talks to the database on its own.

## The helpers [#the-helpers]

`exakit.nb` exports about 110 names, listed in [All commands](/data-scientist/reference). The rules they follow:

* **The connection comes from the kit.** `nb.connect()` opens it from the kit's encrypted store. No helper prints or returns a host, a user or a password.
* **The kit does the work.** Describing a table is the kit's describe service; loading is `exakit data-load`; connecting a source is `exakit connect`. The helpers call these, they do not reimplement them.
* **SQL is shown.** `nb.sql` records the statement, `nb.show_sql()` prints it, and the workflow logs it.
* **Reads are live.** `nb.components()`, `nb.addons()`, `nb.connectors()` and the rest ask the kit when called.

## The guided view [#the-guided-view]

```text
notebook/package/exakit_guide/
  actions.py     every action: one or more lines of exakit.nb code, and its notebook
  session.py     the notebook's namespace the actions run in
  card.py        the widget; a button's code comes from its action
  screens/       one module per page (home, understand, explore, ask, share): UI only
  static/        card.js and card.css: the renderer, no facts
```

`actions.code(id, **values)` is the exact cell text. `actions.run(id, **values)` runs that text in the notebook's namespace and logs it. A screen changes nothing except through `actions.run`, which is why **Code** can always show what a card did.

## Rules the tests enforce [#rules-the-tests-enforce]

* An action's call exists in its notebook's code section, and calls something `exakit.nb` exports.
* No screen names a dataset, connector, add-on or notebook. Those are read from the kit.
* No action shows a secret: a key is bound at run time, never written into the code.
* Every exported helper has a page in these docs, and every link in them leads somewhere.

## Notebooks [#notebooks]

Sources are `notebook/notebooks/<persona>/<NN>_<name>.py` in jupytext percent format. The `.ipynb` and the Marimo version are built from them:

```bash
python3 tools/notebooks.py --marimo            # rebuild
python3 tools/notebooks.py --check --marimo    # fail when a built file is stale
```


# Where things live (/data-scientist/develop/where-things-live)



Everything is under the kit's home, `~/.exasol-starter-kit` (or `EXAKIT_HOME` when set).

| Path                                         | What it holds                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `notebooks/starter-kit-notebooks/<persona>/` | Your copies of the notebooks                                                 |
| `notebooks/marimo/<persona>/`                | The Marimo versions                                                          |
| `descriptors/`                               | Approved column maps, one folder per table, every version kept               |
| `last-dataset`                               | The dataset approved last, which the notebooks follow                        |
| `workflows/<id>.jsonl`                       | Workflow logs                                                                |
| `last-workflow`                              | The workflow started or resumed last                                         |
| `bundles/<workflow id>/`                     | Hand-off bundles, each also as a zip                                         |
| `handoffs/`                                  | Training handoffs for the ML Engineer                                        |
| `exakit.env`                                 | Settings such as the model's id and address                                  |
| `credentials/`                               | Secrets, readable by you only. Never read or print these from a notebook.    |
| `kit/`                                       | The kit copy: scripts, datasets, the notebook package and this documentation |

## In the database [#in-the-database]

| Schema                                                 | What it holds                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `SEMANTIC_CATALOG`, `SEMANTIC_ADMIN`, `SEMANTIC_AGENT` | Exasol Semantic Views: the semantic models built from the approved column maps |
| `SEM_<MODEL>`                                          | A model's published semantic views, queried with Semantic SQL                  |
| `EXAKIT_PREPARED`                                      | Joined views and typed, cleaned views you chose to create                      |
| `VS_<NAME>`                                            | The tables of an external source named `<NAME>`                                |

## What an update touches [#what-an-update-touches]

* A kit notebook you did not edit is refreshed when the kit's version changes.
* A notebook you edited, or a file of your own, is never overwritten.
* A notebook you deleted is not copied back.
* Approved column maps, workflow logs and bundles are yours and are left alone.


# Ask your data (/data-scientist/reference/ask)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

The archived Governed SQL server is not installed. The kit's own model endpoint can draft SQL from an approved
descriptor; no SQL runs until the person approves it. The SQL runs on the launcher's MCP server beside the
database (the sidecar, on loopback), which connects as the dedicated read-only user only - never the notebook's
admin connection or an admin fallback. The notebook sends no password: the sidecar holds the read-only login.

## nb.ask [#ask]

```python
nb.ask(
    dataset: Any,
    question: str,
    proposed_sql: str | None=None,
    *,
    table_description: str | None=None,
    request_timeout: float | None=None,
    max_output_tokens: int | None=None,
) -> Proposal
```

Draft SQL from roles and the user's opted-in model endpoint; `proposed_sql` supports manual drafting.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/02_ask_your_data`

## nb.Proposal [#Proposal]

```python
class nb.Proposal
```

A question with the SQL proposed for it. Nothing runs until `approve()` accepts that exact text; `edit()` replaces
the SQL and removes the approval; `run()` runs the approved text through the kit's read-only service.

| Member                       | What it is  |
| ---------------------------- | ----------- |
| `dataset`                    | `Any`       |
| `question`                   | `str`       |
| `sql`                        | `str`       |
| `assumptions`                | `list[str]` |
| `doubts`                     | `list[str]` |
| `edit(sql: str) -> Proposal` |             |
| `approve() -> Proposal`      |             |
| `run()`                      |             |


# ML Engineer checks (/data-scientist/reference/checks)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

The three things the ML Engineer's notebooks depend on, one check each (ml-engineer/00_quickstart): the database's
Python container answers a smoke UDF with the packages training needs, the MLflow server is reachable, and the bucket
directory is where the kit expects it. Each prints one line - `ok` with what it found, or `FAIL` with the reason
and the fix - and returns True or False, so the notebook shows all three before anything stops.

Nothing here prints a host, a user or a password; an MLflow address is shown without any credentials it holds.

## nb.check_bucket [#check_bucket]

```python
nb.check_bucket(conn=None) -> bool
```

The deployment's bucket directory exists on this machine where the kit says it is, and - given a connection -
a UDF sees it at its /buckets path too (skipped, with a note, when the container check fails).

**Used in:** `ml-engineer/00_quickstart`

## nb.check_container [#check_container]

```python
nb.check_container(
    conn,
    alias: str | None=None,
    packages: tuple[str, ...]=TRAINING_PACKAGES,
) -> bool
```

The container behind `alias` runs a smoke UDF, and it has every package training needs. The line names the
alias probed and the fix for that alias (PYTHON3_ML: exakit udf-use default; PYTHON3: exakit udf-setup), so the
fix installs the container the check looks at. `alias` None is the notebook's default, ml_train.udf_container():
PYTHON3_ML before PYTHON3 from the kit's manifest, EXAKIT_UDF_CONTAINER first; none installed is a FAIL line.

**Used in:** `ml-engineer/00_quickstart`

## nb.check_mlflow [#check_mlflow]

```python
nb.check_mlflow(timeout: float=5.0) -> bool
```

Check the destination runs will really use: configured server, kit server, or local store.

**Used in:** `ml-engineer/00_quickstart`

## nb.check_model_compatibility [#check_model_compatibility]

```python
nb.check_model_compatibility(
    conn,
    model_version: str,
    alias: str='PYTHON3',
    model_path: str='model.pkl',
) -> bool
```

Refuse a pickle whose scikit-learn version differs before any scoring SQL runs.

**Used in:** `ml-engineer/03_score_external_model`

## nb.model_list [#model_list]

```python
nb.model_list(timeout: float=120.0) -> dict[str, Any]
```

What `exakit model list --json` says: bucket_dir (the host folder), udf_root (the path UDFs read it under) and
the models in it. Raises RuntimeError naming why it could not be read.


# Connect, SQL and tracing (/data-scientist/reference/core)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

The connection comes from the kit. Its Jupyter kernel ("Exasol (Starter Kit)") carries two paths: the encrypted
configuration store, and the kit's credential file holding the store's master password, readable by the user only.
These helpers open the database from there, in JupyterLab, Marimo, VS Code or any front end that runs the
kit's notebook Python. Nothing here prints or returns a host, a user or a password.

```python
import exakit.nb as nb
conn = nb.connect()
df = nb.sql(conn, "SELECT * FROM TPCH.NATION")
nb.show_sql()
ds = nb.dataset(conn, "amazon_sales")               # the roles of a dataset, checked against the database
ds = nb.load_own_file("~/data/sales.json", "MY_DATA.SALES", {"entity": "CUSTOMER", ...})   # or your own file
with nb.trace(conn, dataset=ds): ...              # model calls as one trace in your Langfuse (opt-in)
```

The quickstarts' shared steps (check_connection, list_schemas, load_sample, load_source, ...) are in quickstart.py;
the ML Engineer's checks (check_container, check_mlflow, check_bucket) in checks.py.

## nb.confirm_send [#confirm_send]

```python
nb.confirm_send(ds: Dataset, rows: int, answer: str | None=None) -> bool
```

Before sampled rows go to a model endpoint: True at once for a table in the database; for a live source (the
descriptor names a source) it names the source and asks, and only a yes sends. `answer` answers for a script;
with no one to ask (a headless run) the answer is no.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/01_explore`

## nb.connect [#connect]

```python
nb.connect(**kwargs: Any)
```

A pyexasol connection to the local database, opened from the kit's encrypted store, pinned to the database's
TLS certificate once the kit has recorded it. Exasol's usage telemetry stays off unless EXASOL_TELEMETRY_DISABLE
was already set.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/01_explore`, `data-scientist/02_ask_your_data`, `data-scientist/03_share`, `ml-engineer/01_train`, `ml-engineer/02_rust_score`, `ml-engineer/03_score_external_model`

## nb.model_client [#model_client]

```python
nb.model_client()
```

(client, model ID) for EXAKIT_MODEL_ID and EXAKIT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL; EXAKIT_PROVIDER_API_KEY is optional for
servers without authentication. Tracing uses Langfuse's instrumented client for the same endpoint and key.
This interface makes text Chat Completions calls; it does not provide a provider's native API features.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/01_explore`

## nb.model_settings [#model_settings]

```python
nb.model_settings() -> dict
```

Display the chosen model and endpoint without the API key or custom header values; makes no request.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`

## nb.show_sql [#show_sql]

```python
nb.show_sql() -> None
```

Print the last statement sql() ran, so a result can always be traced to the query behind it.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`, `data-scientist/01_explore`, `ml-engineer/00_quickstart`

## nb.sql [#sql]

```python
nb.sql(conn, statement: str, params: dict | None=None)
```

Run a query and return its rows as a pandas DataFrame; the statement is remembered for show_sql().

The rows come over the normal connection rather than pyexasol's HTTP export, which needs the database to connect
back to this machine - not a given through the local VM or Podman.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`, `data-scientist/01_explore`, `ml-engineer/00_quickstart`, `ml-engineer/02_rust_score`, `ml-engineer/03_score_external_model`

## nb.trace [#trace]

```python
nb.trace(
    conn,
    name: str='exakit-notebook',
    dataset: Dataset | None=None,
    sql: str | None=None,
    **metadata: Any,
) -> Iterator[Any]
```

Group the model calls made inside the block into one trace in the user's own Langfuse project, tagged with the
database session, the sample SQL, the workflow id and, given a dataset, its id, descriptor digest and descriptor
version (trace_tags). Opt-in: without LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY and LANGFUSE_BASE_URL (LANGFUSE_HOST,
the SDK 3/4 name, still counts) it says so in one line and does nothing else - no exception, no prompt.

Langfuse SDK 5: the block is one observation (`Langfuse.start_as_current_observation`) and, right inside it, the
trace name, session id, tags and metadata are propagated (`langfuse.propagate_attributes`, a module function in
SDK 5) to it and to every observation opened within, so each call the client model_client() returns makes -
Langfuse's OpenAI drop-in when tracing is on - lands in this one trace with its input, output, token usage and
latency, without changes to the calling code. The span is yielded; the client is flushed when the block ends.
The active workflow's log gets one `trace` line with the trace id (X-1), and when the block ends one line is
printed - `traced: <trace id> (<url or base URL>)` - so the trace can be found in Langfuse. Nothing here prints
or records the secret key.

## nb.tracing [#tracing]

```python
nb.tracing() -> bool
```

Whether LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY and LANGFUSE_BASE_URL (or LANGFUSE_HOST) are all set, so trace()
records to the user's Langfuse.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`

The notebook's Dash Server tool adapter; each call is an MCP tool call. When Dash Server is not installed or
not running, it is installed and started first, the way nb.addon_ready("dash-server") does it (`exakit
marketplace dash-server`, `exakit start dash-server`), with its progress shown: a cell that previews a dashboard

**Used in:** `data-scientist/03_share`
