# Data checks (/data-scientist/reference/data-checks)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

Both are built from the descriptor alone - the key, the label and every column's role - so no column name is typed in
a notebook and the same cell runs on every dataset. Each check is one or two SQL statements, run through nb.sql (so
they are shown and logged like every other query), and each finding is one plain sentence saying what it does to a
result. Nothing is changed in the data: deciding what to do about a finding is the user's.

```python
findings = nb.data_checks(conn, ds)        # Prepare: repeated keys and ids, exact copies, gaps, placeholders, a rare label
leaks = nb.leakage_check(conn, ds)         # Validate: columns whose values (almost) decide the label on their own
```

## nb.data_checks [#data_checks]

```python
nb.data_checks(conn, ds, *, show: bool=True)
```

Prepare: one row per finding - CHECK, COLUMN_NAME, ROWS_AFFECTED, PCT, MEANS - for repeated keys, repeated
identifiers, exact copies of a row, empty cells, placeholder values and a rare label. Prints each finding in one
sentence (`show=False` only returns them); an empty frame means the table passed every check.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/01_explore`

## nb.leakage_check [#leakage_check]

```python
nb.leakage_check(conn, ds, *, show: bool=True) -> list[str]
```

Validate: the columns whose values (almost) decide the label on their own - each a value or values where the
label is (nearly) always 1 or always 0, covering most rows. Such a column is usually written after the outcome
(an order's status once it was cancelled) and makes any model look perfect; leave it out of the features. Returns
those columns (none: the list is empty) and prints why each was flagged.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/01_explore`


# Data map (/data-scientist/reference/data-map)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

```python
data = nb.data_map(connection)      # sample datasets, your loaded files and folders, connected sources
data                                # one table per origin: rows, columns, column map, roles; then the links
data.tables                         # one row per table (a DataFrame)
data.columns                        # one row per column, with its approved role when there is one
data.links                          # joins across tables and origins: declared, found, or a shared key name
```

Three origins, one view:

* \*\*sample\*\*: a dataset the kit ships (`exakit data-load amazon_sales`);
* \*\*local\*\*: your own file or folder (`exakit data-load <path>`, the quickstart's MY_DATA cell);
* \*\*source\*\*: a connected external source, read live through its virtual schema (`exakit connect`).

Roles come from the approved column maps in the kit's store, and the semantic layer is Exasol Semantic Views: a table
that is an entity of a semantic model the kit built says which model (SEMANTIC_CATALOG.ENTITIES). The links are the
approved schema maps' and the multi-source models' (nb.semantic_model). Columns that share a key-like name across
two tables are listed as possible links: a lead to check, never a join made for you. Only metadata is read.

## nb.data_map [#data_map]

```python
nb.data_map(conn, *, include_kit: bool=False) -> DataMap
```

The semantic map of the database: every table by origin (sample, local, source) with its rows, columns,
column-map state and roles, then the links between tables - declared, found by an approved schema map, or a
shared key-like column name across two tables (marked possible). Reads metadata only; returns a DataMap that
shows itself as a table in a notebook. `include_kit` keeps the kit's own schemas in.

## nb.DataMap [#DataMap]

```python
class nb.DataMap
```

What data_map found: tables, columns and links, each a list of dicts; DataFrames through the properties.

| Member                               | What it is                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `table_rows`                         | `list[dict[str, Any]]`                                                          |
| `column_rows`                        | `list[dict[str, Any]]`                                                          |
| `link_rows`                          | `list[dict[str, Any]]`                                                          |
| `tables`                             |                                                                                 |
| `columns`                            |                                                                                 |
| `links`                              |                                                                                 |
| `table(name: str) -> dict[str, Any]` | One table's row, by SCHEMA.TABLE (any case).                                    |
| `roles(name: str) -> dict[str, str]` | \{column: role} of one table's approved column map; empty when it has none yet. |


# Datasets (/data-scientist/reference/dataset)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

```python
ds = nb.dataset(conn, "amazon_sales")                 # a dataset the kit ships, by id
ds = nb.dataset(conn, "~/data/descriptor.yaml")    # a table already in the database, described by a descriptor file
ds = nb.dataset(conn, "~/data/sales.csv")          # your own CSV, Parquet or JSON file, its descriptor beside it
ds.col("label"), ds.text_sql(), ds.fact_table, ds.source
ds.version, ds.status, ds.owner, ds.created, ds.table_digest    # the descriptor's record (schema_version 2)
ds.require_approved("training")                    # a draft stops here with how to approve it
```

The rules are the kit's descriptor rules (`descriptor_rules`, shipped with this package: the 0.2 kit has no Python
package to import them from). It is a copy of tools/descriptor_rules.py, which tools/dataset_check.py uses, and
tests/test_notebook_contents.py holds the two byte-identical. Nothing is guessed: a descriptor that is invalid, or
names a table or column the database lacks, stops the notebook with the reason.

Which descriptor a name resolves to, in order: a path given (a file, or a folder holding descriptor.yaml); for a
data file of your own, `<name>.descriptor.yaml` beside it; for an id, the approved version in the kit's store
(`~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/<SCHEMA>.<TABLE>/current.yaml`, or an older kit's `descriptors/<id>/current`;
descriptor_store), then the descriptor the kit ships under
`data/datasets/<id>/`. `ds.descriptor_path` and `ds.descriptor_origin` say which one was used.

## nb.chosen_dataset [#chosen_dataset]

```python
nb.chosen_dataset(name: str | Path | None=None) -> str
```

The dataset a notebook works on: `name` when it is set; with None, the one approved last in a quickstart (so
picking fraud_transactions there carries on here), else amazon_sales. Says which, and why, in one line.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/01_explore`, `data-scientist/02_ask_your_data`, `data-scientist/03_share`, `ml-engineer/01_train`, `ml-engineer/02_rust_score`, `ml-engineer/03_score_external_model`

## nb.Dataset [#Dataset]

```python
class nb.Dataset
```

A validated descriptor whose every role the database holds, with the SQL names the notebooks build queries from.

| Member                                      | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                                        | `str`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `path`                                      | `Path`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `digest`                                    | `str`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `descriptor`                                | `Any`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `descriptor_path`                           | \`Path                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | None\` |
| `descriptor_origin`                         | `str`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `fact_table`                                | `SCHEMA.TABLE` that one row of analysis comes from.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `source`                                    | The external source's alias when the table is in a virtual schema (a live source), else None - what confirm_send and the quickstart ask about.                                                                                                                  |
| `source_ref`                                | The descriptor's `source` as written: a dataset id, `file:<path>`, `vs:<alias>` (or a schema_version 1 file's bare alias), or None.                                                                                                                             |
| `version`                                   | The descriptor's version: 1 for a first draft or a shipped file; approving writes the next.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `status`                                    | `draft` (proposed, not yet confirmed) or `approved`.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `owner`                                     | Who drafted or approved it (`kit` for a shipped descriptor).                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `created`                                   | When this version was written (ISO-8601), None for a schema_version 1 file.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `table_digest`                              | The digest of the table the descriptor was approved on (its `digest` key, design 2.3: sha256 over the table's name, its columns and types, the row count and an order-independent content hash of the role columns), None until approve computes it.            |
| `current_table_digest(conn) -> str`         | The table's digest as it is now, computed the way approve computed `table_digest`; a value that differs from `table_digest` means the data changed since the descriptor was approved (a virtual table's digest covers its first sample rows and the row count). |
| `drafted_by`                                | `profile` (exakit describe), `shipped` (the kit) or `user` (roles given by hand).                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `evidence`                                  | Per role, the numbers that chose its column (what the profiler recorded; empty for roles given by hand).                                                                                                                                                        |
| `notes`                                     | Per column, a model-written line about it (never decisive; empty without a model).                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `missing`                                   | The roles no column fits, each `{role, reason}`; the notebooks skip what depends on them with the reason.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `require_approved(purpose: str) -> Dataset` | This dataset when its descriptor is approved; a draft raises DescriptorNotApproved saying how to approve it.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `col(role: str) -> str`                     | The column of a single-column role (entity, category, date, label).                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `text_cols() -> list[str]`                  | The text columns, in the descriptor's order; none when no column plays the text role.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `text_sql() -> str`                         | One SQL expression joining the text columns with a space, NULLs as empty; a dataset without text raises ValueError with the descriptor's reason.                                                                                                                |
| `roles() -> list[tuple[str, str]]`          | (role, SCHEMA.TABLE.COLUMN) for every role, for a table the notebook prints.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `has(role: str) -> bool`                    | Whether a column plays `role` (False for one listed under `missing`).                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `group_by() -> tuple[str, str]`             | (role, column) the overviews count rows by: the category, else the entity, else the target - a table with only a key, a text and a 0/1 target has no other group, and counting by that target is its overview.                                                  |
| `tags() -> dict[str, str]`                  | What a trace or an MLflow run records about the data: the dataset and the descriptor's digest (and the source's alias for a live source).                                                                                                                       |

## nb.dataset [#dataset]

```python
nb.dataset(conn, name: str | Path) -> Dataset
```

The dataset `name`, checked against the database: a kit dataset id, a descriptor file or its folder, or a data
file of your own (CSV, Parquet or JSON) with its descriptor beside it, which is loaded first (load_own_file).

**Used in:** `data-scientist/02_ask_your_data`, `data-scientist/03_share`, `ml-engineer/01_train`, `ml-engineer/02_rust_score`, `ml-engineer/03_score_external_model`

## nb.DescriptorNotApproved [#DescriptorNotApproved]

```python
exception nb.DescriptorNotApproved
```

A step that needs an approved descriptor was given a draft; the message says how to approve it.


# Describe a table (/data-scientist/reference/describe)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

```python
d = exakit_nb.describe("AMAZON.ORDER_LINES")    # profile, draft v(n+1), show the table
d.set(PRODUCT="category", ZIP_CODE="identifier")  # corrections, chainable
d.slot(target="TIMELY_RESPONSE")                  # target=None leaves it empty on purpose
ds = d.approve()                                  # check, write, publish; the Dataset read back
```

describe() on a table whose approved descriptor still matches it returns that one (force=True profiles again);
otherwise the table is profiled once, in SQL, and every column gets one of eight roles with the evidence that chose
it; the slots name the columns the notebooks use. show() lists each column with the schema and table it came from,
its type, role, confidence, evidence and note, low confidence first, the slots above (rows() gives the same as dicts;
a notebook renders it as a table). approve() checks every column has a role and none sits in two slots, checks
the table has not changed since it was profiled, writes the next version into the kit's store and rebuilds the
schema's Exasol Semantic Views model with it - the roles become its dimensions, facts and metrics; Semantic Views is
installed first when the database does not have it (a publish that fails leaves the approval standing, and says
why). The active workflow's log gets one line.

The work is the kit's own service, setup/lib/describe_service.py in the kit copy (the one `exakit describe` runs),
loaded from its file and run in this process over the kit's connection; without the kit copy, `exakit describe --json` runs as a child process instead.

The role review (role_picker) speaks the five roles of earlier descriptors - entity, category, date, label, text - so
`roles`, `evidence`, `missing` and `set(role, column)` read and write the matching slots: date is the time
slot and label the target.

## nb.describe [#describe]

```python
nb.describe(
    table_or_dataset: str,
    sample: int=SAMPLE,
    *,
    conn=None,
    id: str | None=None,
    force: bool=False,
) -> Draft
```

Describe `SCHEMA.TABLE` (or a dataset id's table): the approved descriptor when the table still matches it,
else a fresh draft. Uses the connection given, else opens the kit's. Only SELECTs run.

## nb.Draft [#Draft]

```python
class nb.Draft
```

A descriptor proposed for a table (status draft), or the approved one describe() returned.

| Member                                                                                          | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                                                                                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `table`                                                                                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `version`                                                                                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `status`                                                                                        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `slots`                                                                                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `column_roles`                                                                                  |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `roles`                                                                                         | The five roles of earlier descriptors, read from the slots: \{role: column}, \{text: \[column]}.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `evidence`                                                                                      | Per role, the column with its role, confidence and the evidence that chose it, plus the profile's numbers.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `missing`                                                                                       | The roles no column plays, each with the reason the empty slot gives.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `notes`                                                                                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `columns() -> list[str]`                                                                        | The table's columns, in table order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `set(role: str \| None=None, column: str \| list[str] \| None=None, **columns: str) -> Draft`   | `set(COLUMN="role", ...)` gives columns a role (one of the eight); `set("label", "COLUMN")`, the form of earlier descriptors, puts a column in that role's slot.                                                                                                                 |
| `slot(**slots: str \| None) -> Draft`                                                           | Put a column in a slot (key, time, text, target, category, entity), or None to leave it empty on purpose.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `assign(role: str, column: str \| list[str] \| None, reason: str \| None=None) -> Draft`        | The role review's correction: `role` (one of the five) to `column`, or empty with `reason`.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `copy() -> Draft`                                                                               |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `to_dict() -> dict[str, Any]`                                                                   | The descriptor document (a copy).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `to_yaml() -> str`                                                                              |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `save(path: str \| Path) -> Path`                                                               | Write the descriptor as YAML; exakit_nb.dataset(conn, path) reads it back.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `approve(owner: str \| None=None, comments: bool=True, *, conn=None, sample: int \| None=None)` | Approve: every column has a role and none sits in two slots, the table has not changed since it was profiled, the next version is written into the kit's store with current.yaml, and the schema's Exasol Semantic Views model is rebuilt with it (`comments=False` skips that). |
| `rows() -> list[dict[str, str]]`                                                                | One dict per column, low confidence first: the schema and table it came from, its name, type, role, confidence, evidence and note.                                                                                                                                               |
| `show() -> None`                                                                                | Print each column with its schema and table, type, role, confidence, evidence and note, low confidence first, the slots above.                                                                                                                                                   |


# Approved column maps (/data-scientist/reference/descriptor-store)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

Where a user's approved descriptors live. Today: `~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/<SCHEMA>.<TABLE>/current.yaml`
(setup/lib/descriptor/store.py writes it; table_descriptor() finds it by its dataset id). Before that, and still read:
`~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/<id>/` (the kit's home, EXAKIT_HOME
when set) holds one `v<n>.yaml` per version and `current`, a text file with the number of the approved version.
Read-only here: `exakit describe <id> --approve` and `Draft.approve()` write versions; `Dataset` reads the
current one before it falls back to a shipped descriptor.

```python
descriptor_store_dir("amazon_sales")   # ~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/amazon_sales
list_versions("amazon_sales")          # [1, 2]: every v<n>.yaml there, in order
current_version("amazon_sales")        # 2, or None when nothing is approved there
current_descriptor("amazon_sales")     # the v2.yaml path, or None
```

## nb.approved_datasets [#approved_datasets]

```python
nb.approved_datasets() -> list[dict]
```

Every dataset with an approved column map, newest approval first: \{id, table, version, approved_at}.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`

## nb.column_map_versions [#column_map_versions]

```python
nb.column_map_versions(id: str) -> list[dict]
```

Every saved version of a dataset's column map, oldest first: \{version, approved_at, roles, slots, evidence} -
what approving one of them again (RoleReview\.approve) would restore.

## nb.current_version [#current_version]

```python
nb.current_version(id: str) -> int | None
```

The approved version's number from `current`, or None when there is none (or the file does not hold one).

## nb.descriptor_store_dir [#descriptor_store_dir]

```python
nb.descriptor_store_dir(id: str) -> Path
```

The folder that holds the versions of the descriptor `id` (whether or not it exists yet); an id that is not
a dataset id is refused, so no path is built from it.

## nb.list_versions [#list_versions]

```python
nb.list_versions(id: str) -> list[int]
```

The version numbers stored for `id` (every v\<n>.yaml), ascending; empty when none is stored.


# Documentation (/data-scientist/reference/docs)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

```python
nb.docs()                   # the documentation (this notebook's persona section), shown under the cell
nb.docs("descriptor")       # search it for a word
nb.docs(nb.describe)        # one command's page (or nb.docs("describe"))
nb.docs("concepts/descriptor")   # one page, by its address
nb.docs(browser=True)       # in a browser tab instead
```

The documentation is a site of plain files the kit ships (`notebook/docs/site` in the kit copy): pages, styles and
a search index, built ahead of time. This module serves that folder from this Python on this computer only
(the loopback address, a free port) and shows it in a frame under the cell, so reading and searching need no internet, no Node
and no second install. The server starts on the first call and stops with the kernel.

A command's page is found in the site's own list (`commands.json`, written from `exakit.nb`'s `__all__` when the
site is built), so every public helper has one. Anything else is handed to the site's search.

## nb.Docs [#Docs]

```python
class nb.Docs
```

What `nb.docs()` returns: the documentation at `url`. A notebook shows it in a frame under the cell;
`open()` opens it in a browser tab.

| Member           | What it is                            |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `open() -> Docs` | Open the page in the default browser. |

## nb.docs [#docs]

```python
nb.docs(what: Any=None, *, height: int=640, browser: bool=False) -> Docs
```

Open the notebooks' documentation: all of it, one command's page, one page, or a search.

`what` is nothing (the section of the persona whose notebook this is, else the start page), a helper or its name (`nb.describe`, `"describe"`: that command's page),
a page's address (`"concepts/descriptor"`), or any other words (searched, typos forgiven). The result shows
under the cell in a frame `height` pixels tall; `browser=True` opens a browser tab too. Served from this
computer only, from files the kit ships: nothing is fetched from the internet.


# Hand-off bundle (/data-scientist/reference/handoff-bundle)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

```python
bundle = nb.handoff_bundle(connection, dataset)       # ~/.exasol-starter-kit/bundles/<workflow id>/ and .zip
```

The folder holds the approved column map (`descriptor.yaml`), the schema map when there is one
(`schema-map.json`), every query the workflow ran with its digest and row count (`queries.sql`), the workflow log
as it is (`workflow.jsonl`) and a `README.md` that says what the data is, which column map version the numbers rest
on, which questions were approved, which dashboards were published and how to repeat it. Nothing in it is a password:
the log is already written without one, and the connection is the kit's.

This is the Data Scientist's hand-off. The ML Engineer's training handoff (one JSON file with the feature view and the
split, `nb.write_handoff`) is a different thing with its own folder.

## nb.handoff_bundle [#handoff_bundle]

```python
nb.handoff_bundle(
    conn,
    ds: Any,
    workflow_id: str | None=None,
    folder: str | os.PathLike | None=None,
    zip_it: bool=True,
) -> HandoffBundle
```

Write the bundle for `ds` and the workflow (the active one, else the last one on this machine, else none) into
`folder` (default `$EXAKIT_HOME/bundles/<workflow id>/`; a bundle for no workflow is named after the dataset)
and, with `zip_it`, a zip beside it. The active workflow's log gets a `handoff` line with the path.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/03_share`

## nb.HandoffBundle [#HandoffBundle]

```python
class nb.HandoffBundle
```

Where the bundle is and what is in it.

| Member        | What it is  |
| ------------- | ----------- |
| `path`        | `Path`      |
| `zip_path`    | \`Path      | None\` |
| `workflow_id` | \`str       | None\` |
| `files`       | `list[str]` |
| `summary`     | `list[str]` |


# Training handoff (/data-scientist/reference/handoff)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

The handoff from the Data Scientist to the ML Engineer (DS-3 -> ML-3, design 4): one JSON file that holds everything
`01_train` needs to train without opening the descriptor - which descriptor version and digest it came from, a digest
of the data, the feature view built from the roles (as `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` SQL), the label and its positive
class, the training SELECT with a reproducible time split, and the input and output schemas. A descriptor without a date
role has no time split: the handoff is refused with the fix (`split="random"` for a reproducible hash split, or a
date role) - a random split is never silent, and `01_train` refuses one the file does not mark as asked for.

```python
path = nb.write_handoff(conn, ds)          # explore's last cell: ~/.exasol-starter-kit/handoffs/<id>-v<n>.json
handoff = nb.read_handoff("amazon_sales")      # the latest one for that descriptor (or a path, or "<id>-v2")
handoff = nb.handoff_from(conn, ds)         # the same record, built from an approved descriptor, not written
nb.handoff_is_stale(conn, handoff, ds)      # None, or the line that says what changed and what to do
```

The feature view is SQL only - category one-hot over the top-20 values plus OTHER, date -> year / month / ISO day of
week / days since the first date, text -> LENGTH, entity -> frequency - so a model that is linear over these columns can
be scored by Rust on the very same view (ML-5): TF-IDF stays out of it (the client-side model in explore keeps it);
top-k token flags computed in SQL are the deferred next step and are recorded as such in the file. The view is not
created here: the ML quickstart and 01_train create it, with the admin profile.

The file names a table, columns, SQL and digests, never a host, a user or a password; the kit's secret-grep test
covers the folder. A workflow that is active gets one `handoff` line in its log (X-1).

## nb.handoff_from [#handoff_from]

```python
nb.handoff_from(
    conn,
    ds: Dataset,
    label: str | None=None,
    split: str | None=None,
    train_share: float=0.8,
    workflow_id: str | None=None,
    written_by: str=WRITTEN_BY,
) -> dict[str, Any]
```

The handoff record for `ds` as design 4 shapes it, built now and returned, nothing written: the descriptor's
id, version, digest (`digest_kind` says whether it is the table digest or the file's) and source; the data
digest (`data_digest_kind`); the feature view; the label and its positive class (`label` overrides it);
the split (`time` over the date role by default; `split="random"` for a hash split, the only way to get one -
without a date role and without that, a ValueError names the fix; `split.explicit` records the choice) and
`train_share`; the training SQL; input and output schemas. `workflow_id` defaults to the active workflow's.

## nb.handoff_is_stale [#handoff_is_stale]

```python
nb.handoff_is_stale(conn, handoff: dict[str, Any], ds: Dataset) -> str | None
```

None when `handoff` still describes `ds` and its data; else the line 01_train prints before it refuses:
the descriptor's version or digest changed (recomputed from `ds`: the same kind the handoff recorded), or - with
a connection - the data digest no longer matches. The fix is in the line.

**Used in:** `ml-engineer/02_rust_score`

## nb.read_handoff [#read_handoff]

```python
nb.read_handoff(id_or_path: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]
```

The handoff as a dict: from a path to the file, from `<id>-v<n>` (that version's file), or from a descriptor
id (the file with the highest version in the handoffs folder). None there is a FileNotFoundError saying how to
make one.

**Used in:** `ml-engineer/02_rust_score`

## nb.write_handoff [#write_handoff]

```python
nb.write_handoff(
    conn,
    ds: Dataset,
    label: str | None=None,
    split: str | None=None,
    train_share: float=0.8,
    workflow_id: str | None=None,
    written_by: str=WRITTEN_BY,
) -> Path
```

Build the handoff (handoff_from) and write it to `$EXAKIT_HOME/handoffs/<id>-v<n>.json` - the folder 0700,
the file 0600, replaced whole (a temporary file renamed over it) so a reader never sees half of one. The active
workflow's log gets a `handoff` line with the path and the descriptor's id and version. Returns the path.


# All commands (/data-scientist/reference)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

Every notebook starts with `import exakit.nb as nb`. Each name below is one call a cell can make, and the same
call a guided card makes behind its buttons.

```python
import exakit.nb as nb
nb.docs(nb.describe)     # open one command's page from a notebook
```

| Command                                                                                      | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`nb.addon_ready`](/data-scientist/reference/kit-commands#addon_ready)                       | Make an add-on usable from here: install it when it is not (`exakit marketplace <addon>`), start it when it is a service and stopped (`exakit start <addon>`), and say its state and address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`nb.addons`](/data-scientist/reference/kit-facts#addons)                                    | The marketplace's add-ons as `exakit marketplace --list --json` reports them: \{id, name, about, status, installed, version, url}, and `offered`: False for one the kit's catalog does not offer yet (its marketplace/catalog.json says "visible": false, so no marketplace screen lists it).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`nb.ai_clients`](/data-scientist/reference/kit-facts#ai_clients)                            | The AI clients the kit can connect to the database (its MCP adapters), each \{id, name, connected}, with connected from `exakit mcp-status --json`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`nb.approved_datasets`](/data-scientist/reference/descriptor-store#approved_datasets)       | Every dataset with an approved column map, newest approval first: \{id, table, version, approved_at}.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [`nb.ask`](/data-scientist/reference/ask#ask)                                                | Draft SQL from roles and the user's opted-in model endpoint; `proposed_sql` supports manual drafting.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [`nb.check_bucket`](/data-scientist/reference/checks#check_bucket)                           | The deployment's bucket directory exists on this machine where the kit says it is, and - given a connection - a UDF sees it at its /buckets path too (skipped, with a note, when the container check fails).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`nb.check_connection`](/data-scientist/reference/quickstart#check_connection)               | The database answers: its time, this session's id and its version, as one row (and one line).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`nb.check_container`](/data-scientist/reference/checks#check_container)                     | The container behind `alias` runs a smoke UDF, and it has every package training needs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`nb.check_mlflow`](/data-scientist/reference/checks#check_mlflow)                           | Check the destination runs will really use: configured server, kit server, or local store.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`nb.check_model_compatibility`](/data-scientist/reference/checks#check_model_compatibility) | Refuse a pickle whose scikit-learn version differs before any scoring SQL runs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [`nb.chosen_dataset`](/data-scientist/reference/dataset#chosen_dataset)                      | The dataset a notebook works on: `name` when it is set; with None, the one approved last in a quickstart (so picking fraud_transactions there carries on here), else amazon_sales.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`nb.clean_path`](/data-scientist/reference/sources#clean_path)                              | A path pasted into a cell, made usable: quotes and spaces around it, a `file://` link, the shell's backslash escapes (`My\ Data`, from a drag into a terminal) and `~` are undone.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`nb.column_map_versions`](/data-scientist/reference/descriptor-store#column_map_versions)   | Every saved version of a dataset's column map, oldest first: \{version, approved_at, roles, slots, evidence} - what approving one of them again (RoleReview\.approve) would restore.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`nb.components`](/data-scientist/reference/kit-facts#components)                            | The kit's parts as `exakit version --json` reports them: \{id, installed, available, status, add_on, ownership, remedy}, with a status of current, ahead, update_available, available (an add-on not installed) or missing; `available` is the version the kit would install or update to.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`nb.confirm_send`](/data-scientist/reference/core#confirm_send)                             | Before sampled rows go to a model endpoint: True at once for a table in the database; for a live source (the descriptor names a source) it names the source and asks, and only a yes sends.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| [`nb.connect`](/data-scientist/reference/core#connect)                                       | A pyexasol connection to the local database, opened from the kit's encrypted store, pinned to the database's TLS certificate once the kit has recorded it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`nb.connect_source`](/data-scientist/reference/sources#connect_source)                      | Connect an external source as a virtual schema, from a notebook cell.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

| [`nb.connector_inputs`](/data-scientist/reference/kit-facts#connector_inputs)                | What `exakit connect <connector>` asks, from the kit's source engine (`inputs`: what its connect form reads, in the form's order).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

| [`nb.continue_workflow`](/data-scientist/reference/workflow#continue_workflow)               | The workflow already going, without an id to paste: this kernel's, else the one inherited through EXAKIT_WORKFLOW_ID, else the last one started or resumed on this machine (a quickstart starts one); a new one named `name` only when there is none.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
